mainTopic: שבת 48a: Heat-raising residue, רבה's two rebukes at the ריש גלותא's house, moving מוכין used for הטמנה, refilling pillows, and opening a new collar on שבת
overview: This amud opens by finishing an answer from the previous amud. Olive residue (גפת) sends heat up to food resting on it, but sesame residue does not. Next comes a two-part story at the house of the ריש גלותא. First, רבה rebukes a servant for putting cold water on a hot kettle, because that creates new heat (אולודי), unlike stacking urns, which only keeps heat (אוקומי). Second, רבה rebukes the servant for spreading a kerchief over a water vat, because people care about keeping a kerchief dry and will squeeze it, unlike a plain cloth (פרונקא). The גמרא then returns to the משנה, and אביי rules that מוכין used for insulating stay מוקצה, since a person does not give them up just because he had no straw. A ברייתא seems to support אביי, but the גמרא shows it can be read another way. Then רב חסדא allows putting stuffing back into a pillow on שבת, and the גמרא settles a contradiction from a ברייתא: stuffing a new pillow is forbidden, but refilling an old one is allowed. Finally, רב rules that opening a new collar on שבת makes one חייב חטאת, and רב כהנא begins an objection that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Olive residue sends up heat, sesame residue does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer. When food only rests on top of the residue, olive residue gives off heat and sesame residue does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As for causing heat to rise: olive residue causes heat to rise, but sesame residue does not cause heat to rise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer on the previous amud. It explains the difference between גפת of olives and גפת of sesame when it comes to sending heat up to food placed on top.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous discussion had two sources that seemed to contradict each other about sesame residue. The answer splits the topics. For actually wrapping food (הטמנה), both kinds are forbidden. For merely resting food on top, only olive residue is forbidden, because only olive residue gives off rising heat.

keyTerms.meaning: Causing heat to rise. Heat from below warms food that sits on top.
Sesame seeds (here, the pressed sesame residue).
They raise up / they send up.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as saying sesame residue may be used for wrapping food. The difference here is only about food resting on top of the residue. For full הטמנה, both kinds of residue are still forbidden.

phrases.english: Regarding causing heat to rise —
phrases.notes: This names the topic where the two kinds of residue differ.

phrases.english: olive residue causes heat to rise,
sesame residue does not cause heat to rise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer earlier that reconciled two sources about גפת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the topics: wrapping food (הטמנה) vs. food merely resting on top.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might have thought the two sources disagree about sesame residue.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both kinds of residue are forbidden for wrapping food. Only olive residue is forbidden for food resting on top, because only it sends up heat.

steps.title: רבה rebukes a servant for placing cold water on a hot kettle
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רבי זירא visit the ריש גלותא. They see a servant put a jug of cold water on top of a hot kettle, and רבה rebukes him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רבי זירא happened to come to the house of the ריש גלותא. They saw a servant who placed a jug of water on the opening of a kettle. רבה rebuked him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story connected to the topic of heat. This step sets up the scene and רבה's rebuke, which רבי זירא will question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The jug of water was cold, and the kettle below was hot. Resting the jug there would warm the cold water. רבה saw this as forbidden on שבת but did not yet explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, leader of the Jews in Babylonia.
They happened to come / they visited.

phrases.english: Rabba and Rabbi Zeira
happened to come to the house of the Exilarch.
They saw a certain servant
who placed a jug of water
phrases.notes: The water in the jug was cold.

phrases.english: on the opening of a kettle.
phrases.notes: The kettle was full of hot water.

phrases.english: Rabba rebuked him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה וְרַבִּי זֵירָא אִיקְּלַעוּ לְבֵי רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story loosely connected to the topic of giving off heat.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה holds that placing cold water on a hot kettle on שבת is forbidden.

steps.title: רבי זירא asks how this differs from stacking urns
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא challenges רבה. Placing one urn on top of another is allowed, so why should this be any different?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to him: How is this different from placing one urn on top of another urn?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא challenges רבה's rebuke. He compares it to a case that is known to be allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting one hot urn on top of another is permitted on שבת. Here too, a vessel is resting on a hot vessel. So רבי זירא asks why this case should be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: How is it different? (a request to explain a distinction)
An urn or kettle for hot water.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to him:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא מִמֵּיחַם עַל גַּבֵּי מֵיחַם?
phrases.english: How is this different from an urn on top of an urn?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא מִמֵּיחַם עַל גַּבֵּי מֵיחַם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's rebuke from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling that placing the jug on the kettle is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Stacking a vessel on a hot vessel is allowed in the case of urns, so it should be allowed here too.

steps.title: Keeping heat is allowed, creating heat is not
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that stacking urns only keeps heat that is already there. Warming cold water creates new heat.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, he is only keeping heat that already exists. Here, he is creating new heat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers רבי זירא by pointing out the key difference between the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the urn case, the top urn is already hot, and resting it on the lower urn only keeps it warm (אוקומי). In the jug case, cold water is being heated up, which creates new heat (אולודי). Creating heat is like cooking, so it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: He is only keeping (preserving) existing heat.

steps.whatToRemember: The rule is אוקומי מותר, אולודי אסור. Keeping something warm is allowed. Bringing new heat into something cold is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This difference between keeping heat and creating it is a basic principle in the laws of warming food on שבת.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם אוֹקוֹמֵי קָא מוֹקֵים,
phrases.english: He said to him: There, he is merely preserving the heat;
here, he is generating heat.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם אוֹקוֹמֵי קָא מוֹקֵים, הָכָא אוֹלוֹדֵי קָא מוֹלֵיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's challenge from step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any vessel resting on a hot vessel is the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Keeping existing heat is allowed. Creating new heat is forbidden.

steps.title: רבה rebukes the servant for putting a cup on a kerchief over a vat
steps.stepSummary: The same servant spreads a kerchief over a water vat and puts a cup on it. רבה rebukes him again.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then he saw that the servant spread a kerchief over the opening of a vat and placed a cup on it. רבה rebuked him.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues with a second scene. This step sets up the case and רבה's rebuke, which רבי זירא will question next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A kerchief spread over a vat of water, with the drawing cup resting on it, is likely to get wet. רבה does not yet say what the problem is. Step 7 shows it.

keyTerms.meaning: A kerchief (a nicer cloth that people care about).
A cup used for drawing water.

phrases.english: He then saw him
that he spread a kerchief over the opening of a vat
and placed a cup on it.
Rabba rebuked him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר חַזְיֵיהּ דִּפְרַס דַּסְתּוֹדַר אַפּוּמֵּיהּ דְּכוּבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second scene in the same story at the ריש גלותא's house.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה holds that spreading a kerchief over a water vat on שבת is forbidden.

steps.title: רבי זירא asks why
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks רבה for the reason behind this rebuke.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to him: Why?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא asks a simple question: what is wrong with what the servant did?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time רבי זירא does not compare the case to anything. He just wants to know the reason. The answer will come from what the servant does next.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to him: Why?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the rebuke in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What prohibition is involved in spreading a kerchief over the vat.

steps.title: Watch and see: the servant squeezes the kerchief
steps.stepSummary: רבה tells רבי זירא to watch. In the end, the servant squeezes the water out of the kerchief.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Now you will see. In the end, he saw that the servant was squeezing it out.
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of explaining, רבה lets the event show the answer. The servant wrings out the wet kerchief.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was סחיטה (squeezing water out of a cloth), which is a Torah prohibition. Spreading the kerchief led straight to the forbidden act, just as רבה expected.

phrases.english: He said to him: Now you will see.
In the end, he saw that he was squeezing it out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 by showing what happened.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The concern is סחיטה: the wet kerchief will be squeezed out.

steps.title: How is this different from a plain cloth?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא challenges again. Spreading a plain cloth (פרונקא) over a vat is allowed, so why not a kerchief?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: How is this different from a plain cloth?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא accepts the concern about squeezing. But he challenges it from a case where a cloth over a vat is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פרונקא can also get wet over a vat, yet spreading it is permitted. If getting wet leads to squeezing, the same worry should apply there too.

phrases.english: He said to him: How is this different from a cloth?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the concern about squeezing from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that spreading a cloth over a vat is forbidden because it might be squeezed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פרונקא over a vat is allowed even though it can get wet, so the kerchief should be allowed too.

steps.title: People care about a kerchief, not about a plain cloth
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that no one minds if a plain cloth gets wet. People do care about a kerchief, so they will wring it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, he is not particular about it. Here, he is particular about it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה explains why the two cloths are treated differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether we worry about squeezing depends on whether the owner cares about the cloth being wet (קפידא). Nobody bothers to wring out a plain cloth. A kerchief is something a person wants dry, so he is likely to squeeze it.

keyTerms.meaning: He is particular / he cares (about it getting wet).

steps.whatToRemember: We worry about סחיטה only when the person cares that the cloth stays dry. That is why a kerchief is forbidden and a plain cloth is allowed.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם לָא קָפֵיד עִילָּוֵיהּ,
phrases.english: He said to him: There, he is not particular about it;
here, he is particular about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם לָא קָפֵיד עִילָּוֵיהּ, הָכָא קָפֵיד עִילָּוֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between the cases based on how much the owner cares.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any cloth over a vat raises the worry of squeezing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a cloth the owner cares about keeping dry raises the worry of סחיטה.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: not in straw
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's list of materials that may not be used for insulating food.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: And one may not insulate in straw.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a phrase from the משנה. This sets up the question that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists materials that may not be used for הטמנה, even before שבת. The second group, which includes straw and מוכין, is forbidden only when they are moist, because then they add heat. The question that follows is about one of these materials.

keyTerms.meaning: Insulating (wrapping) food to keep it hot.

phrases.english: And not in straw.
phrases.notes: This quotes the opening words of the משנה's list. The list also includes grape residue and soft materials (מוכין).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and returns to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Straw (along with the other materials in this group) may not be used for הטמנה when moist, even before שבת.

steps.title: May insulating scraps be moved on שבת?
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר מתנה asks אביי whether מוכין used for insulating food may be moved on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר מתנה asked אביי: Soft scraps in which a person insulated food, may they be moved on שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question is raised about the מוכין mentioned in the משנה. The question is about whether they may be moved, not about using them to insulate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, loose scraps of material are מוקצה, because they have no use and may not be moved on שבת. The question is whether using them for הטמנה gives them the status of a usable item (כלי), which may be moved.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (introduces a question to a teacher).
Soft scraps of material such as wool or cotton.
To move them (the laws of מוקצה).

steps.confusionAlert: This question is not about whether you may insulate with מוכין on שבת. The question is about moving the scraps on שבת, which is a question of מוקצה.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה מֵאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Mattana asked Abaye:
Soft scraps in which he insulated food,
what is the law about moving them on Shabbat?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה מֵאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a question about the מוכין mentioned in the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether מוכין used for הטמנה become a usable item that may be moved, or stay מוקצה.

steps.title: אביי Rules the Stuffing Stays Set Aside
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that מוכין used for insulating may not be moved. The owner never truly gave them up for that use.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Just because he has no basket of straw, will he get up and give up his basket of soft materials?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב אדא בר מתנה's question. The answer is no, the מוכין may not be moved on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person would normally insulate food with cheap straw. He used his valuable מוכין only because he had no straw at that moment. He does not want them used for other things that might ruin them, so they keep their status as מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: gets up and gives up (renounces) ownership or use
an item set aside, which may not be moved on שבת

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets out the key idea of the סוגיא. A one-time emergency use does not change what an item is set aside for.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְכִי מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ
phrases.english: He (Abaye) said to him: Just because he does not have
phrases.notes: אביי is answering רב אדא בר מתנה.

phrases.english: a basket of straw,
does he get up and give up
phrases.notes: This is a rhetorical question. Of course he does not!

phrases.english: a basket of soft materials?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְכִי מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ קוּפָּה שֶׁל תֶּבֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מוכין may not be moved. Using them out of necessity does not show that the owner gave them up for insulating.

steps.title: A ברייתא Seems to Support אביי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that a ברייתא backs up אביי. It says one may insulate with wool materials but may not move them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this supports him? One may insulate in woolen fleece, in combed wool, in strips of purple wool, and in soft materials, but one may not move them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to prove אביי right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא allows insulating with these wool materials. In the same breath it says they may not be moved. That sounds exactly like אביי: even after they were used for insulating, they stay מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: shall we say this supports him?

phrases.english: Shall we say that this supports him:
One may insulate in woolen fleece,
in combed wool, and in strips of purple wool,
and in soft materials, but one may not move them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to support אביי's answer from a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's ruling that מוכין used for insulating stay מוקצה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that allows insulating with wool materials and then says they may not be moved.

steps.title: The ברייתא Means Unused Materials
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברייתא's ban on moving refers to materials that were not used for insulating.
steps.simpleTranslation: If that is the reason, it is no proof. This is what it means: if he did not insulate with them, one may not move them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from the ברייתא by reading it a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא can be read as two separate rules. First, you may insulate with these materials. Second, if you did not insulate with them, they may not be moved. On this reading, the ברייתא says nothing about materials that were used, so it does not prove אביי right.

keyTerms.meaning: it is no proof; that is not the point

steps.confusionAlert: This does not prove אביי wrong. It only shows that the ברייתא is not a proof for him.

phrases.english: If because of this, it is no proof,
this is what it is saying:
if he did not insulate with them,
one may not move them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the ברייתא is rejected, not אביי's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ban on moving may refer only to materials that were never used for insulating.

steps.title: Why Would the ברייתא State Something Obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new reading. If it is about unused materials, it is obvious that they may not be moved.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is it coming to tell us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new reading of the ברייתא from step 14. It says that reading makes the ברייתא state something obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wool and stuffing kept for sale or for making things are clearly set aside. A ברייתא should not need to teach that unused materials like these are מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: what is there to say? (it is obvious)

phrases.english: If so, what is there to say?!
phrases.notes: In other words, it is obvious.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reinterpretation given in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the ברייתא is talking about unused materials.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading makes the ברייתא teach something obvious, and a ברייתא does not state the obvious.

steps.title: One Might Think They Are Fit to Sit On
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's point is not obvious. One might have thought the materials can be used as a seat and may therefore be moved.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said they are fit to sit on, so it teaches us that they may not be moved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It explains that the ברייתא is teaching something real.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Soft wool could be used as a seat, so you might think it counts as a usable item that may be moved. The ברייתא teaches that it is still מוקצה, because the owner wants to keep it clean and set aside for its own purpose.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי rules that מוכין used for insulating stay מוקצה, because a person does not give up his valuable materials just because straw was missing. The ברייתא is not a proof for him, since it may mean unused materials. Even unused materials needed to be taught, because one might have thought they are usable as seats.

phrases.english: You might have said
they are fit to sit on,
so it teaches us that they may not be moved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows the teaching is not obvious, because one could have reasoned otherwise.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the materials can be sat on, they count as usable items and may be moved.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even so, unused wool materials remain מוקצה and may not be moved.

steps.title: רב חסדא allows putting stuffing back into a pillow on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that stuffing which fell out of a pillow may be put back on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא permitted putting stuffing back into a pillow on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by reporting a ruling of רב חסדא. He allows a person to put stuffing back into a pillow on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is stuffing that fell out of a pillow. רב חסדא says it may be returned on שבת. The next step will test this ruling against a ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda permitted
returning stuffing into a pillow
on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new, related topic about stuffing (soft materials) after the discussion of insulating materials.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may put stuffing back into a pillow on שבת.

steps.title: רב חנן בר חסדא challenges רב חסדא from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says one may not put stuffing into a pillow or cushion, even on יום טוב, and certainly not on שבת. This seems to contradict רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנן בר חסדא raised an objection to רב חסדא from a ברייתא: One may untie a collar on שבת, but one may not open a new one. And one may not put stuffing into a pillow or a cushion on יום טוב, and certainly not on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנן בר חסדא quotes a ברייתא to attack רב חסדא's ruling. The ברייתא clearly forbids putting stuffing into a pillow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא forbids putting stuffing into a pillow even on יום טוב, which is more lenient than שבת. So on שבת it is surely forbidden. That seems to directly contradict רב חסדא, who allowed it.

keyTerms.meaning: he raised an objection to him (from a תנאי source)
the neck opening (collar) of a garment
we may open (for the first time)

steps.confusionAlert: The first part of the ברייתא, about the collar, is not the point of the challenge. The challenge comes from the second part, about putting stuffing into a pillow.

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב חָנָן בַּר חִסְדָּא לְרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Chanan bar Chisda raised an objection to Rav Chisda:
One may untie the neck opening on Shabbat,
but one may not open it (for the first time).
And one may not put soft stuffing

phrases.aramaic: לֹא לְתוֹךְ הַכַּר וְלֹא לְתוֹךְ הַכֶּסֶת
phrases.english: not into a pillow and not into a cushion

phrases.aramaic: בְּיוֹם טוֹב, וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: on a Festival, and needless to say, on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב חָנָן בַּר חִסְדָּא לְרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב חסדא's ruling from step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's permission to put stuffing back into a pillow on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא forbids putting stuffing into a pillow even on יום טוב, so on שבת it must be forbidden. That contradicts רב חסדא.

steps.title: New pillows versus old pillows
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא forbids stuffing a new pillow. רב חסדא allows refilling an old pillow.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This (the ברייתא) is about new pillows, and that (רב חסדא) is about old pillows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It shows that the ברייתא and רב חסדא are talking about two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stuffing a new pillow for the first time turns it into a finished, usable item. That counts as making a new כלי, so it is forbidden. Putting stuffing back into an old pillow it fell out of only restores it, so רב חסדא allows it.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is with new ones, that is with old ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא בְּחַדְתֵי הָא בְּעַתִּיקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 18 by splitting the cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): new pillows versus old pillows.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to forbid putting stuffing into any pillow, which would contradict רב חסדא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא forbids stuffing new pillows, because that makes a new כלי. רב חסדא permits refilling old pillows.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the new-versus-old split
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא forbids putting stuffing into a pillow but allows putting fallen stuffing back, even on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was also taught in a ברייתא: One may not put stuffing into a pillow or a cushion on יום טוב, and certainly not on שבת. If the stuffing fell out, one may put it back on שבת, and certainly on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same split the גמרא just made. This supports the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא has two parts. Putting stuffing into a pillow for the first time is forbidden. Putting back stuffing that fell out is allowed. This matches the difference between new and old pillows, which supports רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: it was also taught this way (a supporting ברייתא)

steps.confusionAlert: Notice that the 'needless to say' wording flips. For the ban, it says 'יום טוב, and certainly שבת,' because שבת is stricter. For the permission, it says 'שבת, and certainly יום טוב,' because whatever is allowed on שבת is surely allowed on יום טוב.
steps.whatToRemember: Stuffing a new pillow for the first time is forbidden on שבת and יום טוב. Putting back stuffing that fell out of an existing pillow is allowed, even on שבת.

phrases.english: It was also taught so:
One may not put soft stuffing

phrases.aramaic: לֹא לְתוֹךְ הַכַּר וְלֹא לְתוֹךְ הַכֶּסֶת
phrases.english: not into a pillow and not into a cushion

phrases.aramaic: בְּיוֹם טוֹב, וְאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: on a Festival, and needless to say, on Shabbat.
If they fell out, one may put them back on Shabbat,
and needless to say, on a Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 19 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The split between stuffing a new pillow (forbidden) and refilling an old one (permitted).
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that forbids first-time stuffing but permits putting back stuffing that fell out (נשרו).

steps.title: Opening a new collar on שבת makes one liable for a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that someone who opens a new collar on שבת is חייב חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Someone who opens a neck opening on שבת is חייב חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the collar case from the first ברייתא. It brings רב's ruling on how serious opening a new collar is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא said only that one may not open a new collar. רב adds that doing so is a real Torah-level מלאכה, so the person is חייב חטאת. Cutting open the collar makes the garment ready to wear, and that counts as finishing a כלי.

keyTerms.meaning: liable to bring a sin-offering (a Torah-level violation done by mistake)

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling shows that finishing an item so it becomes usable counts as a real מלאכה on שבת. The same idea explains why stuffing a new pillow is forbidden.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
One who opens a neck opening on Shabbat
is liable to bring a sin-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the collar case mentioned in the ברייתא of step 18 and tells us how serious it is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening a new collar on שבת is a Torah-level מלאכה, and one who does it by mistake is חייב חטאת.

steps.title: רב כהנא opens a strong objection to רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that רב כהנא strongly objects to רב's ruling that opening a new collar on שבת makes one חייב חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא strongly objected to it:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line: the גמרא tells us that רב כהנא is about to attack רב's ruling. The actual argument comes in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'לַהּ' ('to it') points back to the ruling just quoted: opening a new collar on שבת makes one חייב חטאת. The phrase מתקיף לה signals a forceful challenge based on reasoning, not just a request for clarification. So we should expect רב כהנא to show why רב's ruling seems hard to accept.

keyTerms.meaning: Strongly objects to it; introduces a forceful, reasoning-based challenge
רב כהנא, an אמורא who raises the objection
The neck opening (collar) of a garment; the subject of רב's ruling being challenged

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for the objection itself here. This line only announces that an objection is coming; the actual argument appears in the next line of the גמרא.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana strongly objected to it:
phrases.notes: 'It' refers to רב's ruling about opening a new collar on שבת (Step 21).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a challenge against the ruling of רב stated in Step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that one who opens a new collar on שבת is חייב חטאת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Not stated yet; this line only announces the objection. Its content comes in the next line of the גמרא.
